[🧵] Typhoon Molave '20 (Quinta) reached its C3 peak before striking Vietnam. Beforehand, Molave hit the Philippines with damaging winds & flash flooding. Agriculture suffered badly after multiple storms prior. A yacht off of Batangas 🇵🇭 sank, killing a few people. 

Then Molave brought more flooding into 🇻🇳 & neighboring Cambodia & Thailand. 🇰🇭 had dozens killed in its floods. 🇻🇳 also had dozens killed & the storm became the 9th costliest TC in the country's history. 

Overall, Molave killed 71-117 & both names were retired & being replaced w/ Narra & Querubin respectively. [1/2]

data.text:
Last night I tried to go on a run. I’m in an area that is the opposite of walkable. I googled “running trails near me” like I always did everywhere in the US and found myself over 5k from the nearest “trail” according to google. I thought to myself: it can’t be that bad! and I’m terrified of getting in another car since I was extorted at the airport… so I thought I’d just run all the way to the nearest “trail” — Quezon City Circle. Historic landmark according to google. Great. Will be good to see. It’s 4 or 5 PM on a Monday. Yes there will be traffic but who cares, I thought!

I thought wrong. Firstly, the Maps apps don’t really work out here because the Satellites that control them don’t reach these pacific islands in the middle of nowhere very well, so every third turn I discover I turned wrong because the pointer icon was in the wrong place, so the result of this is a tall white man jogging confidently down the third world shithole streets of Manila holding his iPhone 13 Pro which is leading him in the wrong direction over and over, onto the highway and over tall bridges and I’m often stepping over what must be human feces everywhere all over the place…

The people watch me run by like I’m a reindeer. They can’t fathom it. I’ve been here for maybe 72 hours, have not seen another white person. I am not kidding. As I run by, the people shout at me: HI SIR! HEY SIR! HELLO! Not hookers—just impoverished street people. But they’re not homeless, they just post up outside their shacks with their tables and their fruit and their kids and their weird dogs that all walk around like they’re on heroin, the fucking cats and dogs around here are like nothing I’ve ever seen in the US, I don’t know why they all have that malnourished malaise about them, it’s kind of sad but every time I see one I can’t help but smile, laugh.

The little kids learn from their parents that when you see a white person, what you’re supposed to do is shout at him, stop him, hold out your cup and ask him for money. I’m not sure their parents explicitly tell them this, they probably just watch and learn, absorb it like kids do. At the start of my Final Destination-esque Iron Man Run from Cubao up to Quezon Circle, out of the slums and onto the highway, these little bug-kids saw me running by and tried to stop me. They threw themselves in front of my body like football players. I juked them out and sprinted faster, my legs are much much longer than theirs are so I quickly lost them. I hope they starve. No I don’t. The toxic polluted air is infecting my typically good-natured heart.

Google Maps should’ve given me a warning: THIS IS NOT THE PLACE TO GO FOR A JOG. YOU ARE RUNNING ON THE THIN EDGE OF A BUSY HIGHWAY IN RUSH HOUR TRAFFIC IN A THIRD WORLD COUNTRY. WHAT ARE YOU DOING YOU STUPID FUCK — but there was no such warning. Gemini is not so advanced.

Instead it just led me along, as I quickly realized that “running” isn’t really a thing here, if you’re Running in the less-developed part of Manila, you’re typically running FROM something, so people stared at me like I was some sort of fugitive. I was dressed in typical western jogger running clothes, short shorts and a well-fitting t-shirt, I probably looked like a Lululemon Ad. Most young women I passed looked starstruck. I have impeccable form, I’ve been running almost every day for many many years. I experienced that familiar runners’ high, that endless outpouring of energy which seemed to never ever end. Up and down hills, through slums and back alley streets, hopelessly relying on my old pal google maps to lead me to a place that we first-worlders might barely consider “walkable.”

I never got there, to Quezon Circle. After maybe 40 minutes of running hard dodging brown people who could not believe what they were seeing I made it up to the University, which is almost pretty much across the street from my intended destination. Thousands of Filipino College students… (or were they highschoolers?) waiting for buses, getting picked up, walking from class, security guards eyeing me with either curiosity or suspicion, I didn’t look back to see, girls looking at me like they tend to do, I finally get to the place I routed to and it is on the other side of an uncrossable street. 10 lane freeway. No crosswalks, no lights, just a sea of buses and cars. Welp I guess I’m not seeing Quezon Circle. This journey was not meant to be walked. I ran well over 5k uphill to get here and now and I’m going to have to run 5k back. I’m pretty tired but runners’ high is real so I just kept going…

The real kicker was the air pollution. I could start to feel the toxicity in my lungs, especially every time I got close to a car, I can still feel some drip in my throat this morning, I started to understand why most of the street-people look so sickly and the dogs move like they’re underwater… the pollution in the air is slowly killing them. I started to realize why there are just about ZERO big strong guys who look like they lift around here, maybe it’s just not part of the culture but I swear it is something in the air and water, probably something in the genetics too, they are a totally skinny race. Just about NO ONE is overweight, everyone is either malnourished or barely decently fit.

But I won’t get a cab. I’ve only got a 500 Peso bill in my pocket (a whopping $9 USD) and I know that’s far too much for a 20min ride home, and honestly I don’t want to deal with another person on the street like this if I can help it. My phone is at 15% battery but I’m sure that’s enough, in low power mode, I thank my former self for buying a new (used) phone before I came here so I wouldn’t be tethered to a charger 24/7 any more. Now it’s dark. Time to run all the way back home.

The run home was just as if not more treacherous. The map sent me on a completely different route, off the highway and through lots of back streets that reminded me of Hawaii. The pollution really started to bother me, I would stop every kilometer or so to catch my breath and go “fuck, oh fuck, fuck” and sometimes laugh at the absurdity of it all. It’s raining now and you’d think that would wash the poison fumes away but somehow it only made it worse. So now my phone’s dying, it’s dark, raining, pollution infecting my sensitive young lungs, weaving through bugpeople for 30-40 more minutes of cardiovascular torture to get back home.

Finally get back to Mall Area where I am staying. Soaking drenched sweating tired just a defeated wet rat of a man. Head into mall to get food so I can bring the food home and eat my slopmeal in peace. Settle for Panda Express, the pollution has made me wary of the food on the streets. Give me something nice and processed my body knows. Find the Panda Express. Get eyefucked by a ton of filipina girls on the way in. It never gets old. Order slop. Pay like $7 USD. Take it home in the rain, so very close.

On the way home, walk-jogging through the rain with my Panda Express bag, I dropped my room key out of my pocket as I was crossing the street. Apparently. Because I heard this voice behind me: HEY SIR!! SIRR!! I braced myself: god some street urchin begging for money again, just let me go home, then I turn around to shoo her off and it’s a short fat college girl. She says “I think you dropped this!” And she’s holding up my key. Oh my god… I look at her like she’s the love of my life. Thank you, thank you so much. She looks at me back, in love, so thankful to have helped me. That would have been an insanely horrible night, if i got locked out of that building. Sleeping outside in Manila, god no. I thanked her with so much love and turned back home.

Wasted many hours texting girls on phone. Responding to messages takes so much time after I’ve shared a good post. I said I wouldn’t get caught up DMing females again but it’s impossible to resist. I’m still adjusting to the change in scenery.

Basically I just chose the wrong area. Quezon City. Re-routing. Re-routing. Re-routing.
